title: Astra and Sol WSI methods and diagnostic outcomes
claim: Five Astra medium and seven revised Sol xhigh WSI conditions produced valid artifacts but uneven task-specific reference agreement. The closest shared endpoint is HuBMAP recall (86/99 released polygons in each run), while TIGER instructions and mask assistance, CAMELYON lesion grouping/case set, and HiESD output grain changed. Sol gave empty answers on two positive CAMELYON slides. These observations locate concrete workflow and task-design limits but cannot isolate a model effect or establish population or clinical performance.
limitations: One selected slide per source, or three fixed TIGER ROIs, and one stochastic attempt per condition do not estimate population performance, clinical validity or model ranking. Public-data pretraining exposure is unknown.

The Sol round changed model and effort alongside task instructions, scoring conventions, case set and method. HuBMAP reference recall is endpoint compatible only; TIGER is diagnostic; CAMELYON and HiESD scores are not numerically comparable across rounds.
Harbor reward validates answer shape, not pathology accuracy. Two early Sol and one Astra transport attempts ended before image analysis and retain no verdict.

HuBMAP unmatched points lack pathology adjudication; TIGER supplied masks carry evaluated tissue labels; CAMELYON lesion grouping is a study rule and its negative is one control; HiESD XML is sparse and its fixed patches were selected using private annotations.
Logged crop containment does not prove visual attention. Source-centered post-hoc crops remove the search task and cannot certify pathology labels.
